text:
Riley: Quick UX review for the chart key. Goals: reduce horizontal clutter, keep mapping obvious, and make outlier behavior discoverable. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/unique/compact-key-v2

Priya: Accessibility: don't hide names entirely. Proposed: compact inline key with swatch + 3-char abbrev, plus a single "Show full key" button. Button must be a real <button aria-expanded="false"> and announce state to SRs.

Devon: Units: show full unit label under the axis when space allows (e.g., "Requests per minute"), but use compact tick marks. Tooltip shows long form. Also add aria-label for ticks: visual "1.2K" -> SR "1,200 requests per minute".

Kai: Outliers: show de-emphasized off-chart markers and a small "+n" badge top-right when points are clipped. Badge is focusable button with aria-label like "3 outliers hidden. Press Enter to include". Clicking expands y-axis.

Priya: Keyboard details:
- Compact key toggle: Enter opens drawer; move focus into list.
- Legend items: Arrow keys navigate, Space toggles visibility.
- Debounce aria-live updates for state changes to avoid spam (200-300ms).

Riley: Visual notes: add caret on toggle, increase hit target to 40px, show inline search when series >8, fall back to stacked legend under chart on very narrow panels.

Devon: Smoothing: move to overflow (advanced) menu with short help text "Smooth lines to emphasize trend; may hide spikes." Default OFF for perf charts.

qa-bot: Reminder: include keyboard + screenreader checks in acceptance criteria. Visual regression will run on PRs linked to figma.

Riley: Accepted. @Priya can you post the exact ARIA strings? @Devon can you prototype formatNumberAccessible and the badge behavior? We'll reconvene after the prototype. :thumbsup:
